A Somali scholar and poet who'd memorized the entire Quran, he founded the Dervish movement against British, Italian, and Ethiopian colonizers — and the British insultingly dubbed him the 'Mad Mullah.' Who was he?
Muḥammad ibn 'Abdallāh Hassan: Somali Jihadist and anti-colonialist leader (1856–1920)
A Florentine diplomat of the Italian Renaissance, this man wrote a famous political treatise published only after his death and is often called the father of modern political science — who was he?
Niccolò Machiavelli: Florentine statesman, diplomat, and political theorist (1469–1527)

Codenamed 'Hero' by the CIA and 'Yoga' by MI6, this Soviet military intelligence colonel's tips about missile installations helped the US spot Soviet weapons in Cuba and navigate the missile crisis without war — who is he?
Oleg Penkovsky: British spy in the USSR (1919–1963)
This prince of Troy, also called Alexander, ran off with Helen and sparked a decade-long war, then later fired the arrow that killed the mighty warrior Achilles — who is he?
Paris (mythology): Trojan prince, second husband of Helen of Troy.
Hailed as "the Lion of Verdun" for leading France to victory in that nine-month WWI battle, this marshal later headed the collaborationist Vichy regime — who is it?
Philippe Pétain: French general and dictator (1856–1951)
Proclaimed by Hitler from Prague Castle on 16 March 1939, this partially annexed Nazi territory covered the Czech lands after their occupation — which entity?
Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia: Territory of Nazi Germany (1939–1945)
Founded in 1997 by Lalu Prasad Yadav, this Bihar-based political party built its support among Other Backward Classes, Dalits, and Muslims — which party?
Rashtriya Janata Dal: Political party in India. The Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD, lit. 'National People's Party') is an Indian political party, mainly based in the Indian state of Bihar.
This former Navy SEAL took part in the 2011 raid that killed Osama bin Laden and later stirred controversy by claiming he alone fired the fatal shot — who is he?
Robert J. O'Neill: US Navy SEAL (born 1976)

Over three days in September 1982, Lebanese Forces militiamen — backed by the IDF — killed thousands of mostly Palestinian and Shia civilians in a Beirut neighbourhood and adjacent refugee camp; what is this atrocity called?
Sabra and Shatila massacre: 1982 mass murder of civilians in Beirut, Lebanon.
This Finnish lawyer chaired the National Coalition Party from 1994 to 2001 and later served as president from 2012 to 2024, defeating Pekka Haavisto in a 2012 runoff — who is he?
Sauli Niinistö: President of Finland from 2012 to 2024. Sauli Väinämö Niinistö (born 24 August 1948) is a Finnish politician who served as the president of Finland from 2012 to 2024.
After serving as Islam Karimov's prime minister, this politician became president of Uzbekistan in 2016 and later chaired the Organization of Turkic States — who is he?
Shavkat Mirziyoyev: President of Uzbekistan since 2016. Shavkat Miromonovich Mirziyoyev (born 24 July 1957) is an Uzbek politician who has served as the second president of Uzbekistan since 2016.
Depicted in the Buddhist wheel of existence, these realms — from gods and humans to hungry ghosts and hell — are where beings are reborn according to their karma. What is it called?
Six Paths: Concept in Buddhist cosmology.
His was the longest reign of any Ottoman sultan, taking Belgrade in 1521 and Rhodes in 1522 and shattering Hungary's army at Mohács in 1526 — who was this sultan?
Suleiman the Magnificent: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire (1520–1566)
This brief conflict ran from June 27 to July 7, 1991, ending when the Brioni Accords settled Slovenia's break from Yugoslavia — what was it called?

Ten-Day War: 1991 Slovenia-Yugoslavia conflict. It was fought between the Slovenian Territorial Defence and the Slovenian National Police Force on one side, and the Yugoslav People's Army on the other.

Nominated in 2019 by Alexander Gauland to become co-chair of Germany's far-right AfD alongside Alice Weidel, this Bundestag member is known for pro-Russian, eurosceptic foreign-policy views. Who is he?
Led by Gamal Abdel Nasser, this short-lived political union merged Egypt and Syria from 1958 until Syria seceded in 1961, though Egypt kept the name until 1971 — which state?
United Arab Republic: Sovereign state in the Middle East (1958–1971)
Held hostage by the Ottomans as a boy, this three-time Voivode of Wallachia is honored as a Christian hero in Romania for fighting the empire. Who is he?
Vlad the Impaler: 15th-century ruler of Wallachia.

Designed by Irish-born architect James Hoban in the Neoclassical style after a Dublin mansion, this building at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue has been home to every U.S. president since John Adams in 1800 — name this residence?
White House: Residence and workplace of the US president.

After leading an outnumbered army to victory at the Battle of Julu and toppling the Qin, this warlord carved China into Eighteen Kingdoms and founded the short-lived state of Western Chu — who was he?
Xiang Yu: Warload of Western Chu of China (c. 232–202 BC)
As the first Premier of the People's Republic of China, he helped orchestrate Richard Nixon's landmark 1972 visit while also serving as foreign minister during the 1950s — who is he?
Zhou Enlai: Premier of China from 1949 to 1976.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Georges Dumézil (born 1898) is the earliest of the four. Dumézil is well known for his formulation of the trifunctional hypothesis on Proto-Indo-European mythology and society.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Which of these four began earliest?
Python (programming language) (founded 1991) is the earliest of the four. Python supports multiple programming paradigms but with an emphasis on object-oriented programming and dynamic typing.
Which of these four dates back furthest?

Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four. Fortran (formerly FORTRAN) is a third-generation, compiled, imperative programming language designed for numeric computation and scientific computing.
Pick the astronomer from these four.
Galileo Galilei is an astronomer. Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Blaise Pascal is a mathematician. Blaise Pascal (19 June 1623 – 19 August 1662) was a French mathematician, physicist, inventor, philosopher, and Catholic writer.
What is the atomic number of Unbinilium?
Unbinilium, also known as eka-radium or element 120, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has symbol Ubn and atomic number 120.
What is the atomic number of Arsenic?
Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
In what year was Ted Kaczynski born?
Ted Kaczynski: The FBI used the case identifier UNABOM (University and Airline Bombing) before his identity was known, resulting in the media naming him the "Unabomber".
In what year was Steve Wozniak born?
Steve Wozniak: In 1976, he co-founded Apple Computer (now Apple Inc.) with his early business partner Steve Jobs.
In what year was Dmitri Mendeleev born?
Dmitri Mendeleev: The synthetic element mendelevium is named in his honor.
In what year did Ptolemy die?
Ptolemy: The first was his astronomical treatise now known as the Almagest, originally entitled Mathēmatikḗ Syntaxis (Μαθηματικὴ Σύνταξις, 'Mathematical Treatise').
In what year did Al-Khwarizmi die?
Al-Khwarizmi: Few biographical details are known about al-Khwarizmi's life.
In what year was Nitrogen discovered?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
Which company manufactures Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk?
Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk: Skunk Works. It was the first operational aircraft to be designed with stealth technology.
In which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21 based?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21: Soviet Union. Approximately 60 countries across four continents have flown the MiG-21, and it still serves many nations seven decades after its maiden flight.
Who is credited with discovering Triangulum Australe?
Triangulum Australe: Américo Vespucio. Triangulum Australe is a small constellation in the far Southern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Ichthyosaurus?
Ichthyosaurus: Mary Anning. It is among the best known ichthyosaur genera, as it is the type genus of the order Ichthyosauria.
Who is credited with discovering Theobroma cacao?
Theobroma cacao: Christopher Columbus. Theobroma cacao (cacao tree or cocoa tree) is a small (6–12 m (20–39 ft) tall) evergreen tree in the Malvaceae family.
Who is credited with discovering Krypton?
Krypton: William Ramsay. Krypton (from Ancient Greek: κρυπτός, romanized: kryptos 'the hidden one') is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

A German-born theoretical physicist best known for developing the theory of relativity, his mass–energy formula E=mc2 comes from special relativity and has been called "the world's most famous equation." Born in 1879, who won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics?
Albert Einstein (14 March 1879 - 18 April 1955) was a German-born theoretical physicist best known for developing the known theory of relativity.
Famed for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, this French mathematician was also a principal founder of the secretive Bourbaki group — who was he?
André Weil (6 May 1906 - 6 August 1998) was a French mathematician, known for his foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry.
This mid-sized zodiac constellation, sitting between Pisces and Taurus, has represented a ram since late Babylonian times — though its stars once formed a farmhand. Which one is it?
Aries (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac. It is located in the Northern celestial hemisphere between Pisces to the west and Taurus to the east.

Manufactured by a Turkish company and credited largely to a former MIT graduate, this medium-altitude combat drone has become one of the most exported unmanned aircraft of its era — what aircraft (family) is it?
Baykar Bayraktar TB2 is a family of medium-altitude long-endurance (MALE) unmanned combat aerial vehicles (UCAV) capable of remotely controlled or autonomous flight operations.
Native to India and Nepal, this medium-sized antelope sports a striking two-tone coat, with males growing corkscrew horns up to 75 cm long. Which animal is it?
Blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal.
An Austrian-born psychologist who directed Chicago's Orthogenic School, he was an early and controversial writer on autism whose ideas grew out of Freud — who was he?

Bruno Bettelheim (August 28, 1903 - March 13, 1990) was an Austrian-born American psychologist, scholar, public intellectual and writer who spent most of his academic and clinical career in the United States.

This group of diseases directly affecting the heart muscle itself may show few symptoms early on but can progress to heart failure, irregular heartbeat, and an increased risk of sudden cardiac death — what condition is it?
Cardiomyopathy is a group of primary diseases of the heart muscle. In dilated cardiomyopathy the ventricles enlarge and weaken.

Used to disinfect skin before surgery, sterilize surgical tools, treat oral yeast infections, and keep urinary catheters clear, this antiseptic compound comes as a gluconate or acetate salt — what is it?
Chlorhexidine is a disinfectant and antiseptic which is used for skin disinfection before surgery and to disinfect surgical instruments.

With just two living species — the Sunda and Philippine varieties — these Southeast Asian gliders are arboreal primatomorphs more closely related to primates than to any other animal — what is this group called?
Colugo are arboreal gliding primatomorphs that are native to Southeast Asia.
Usually viral and often worse at night, this childhood respiratory infection swells the windpipe to produce a barking, brassy cough and noisy breathing — what's the condition?
This annual herb in the celery family, native to North Africa and West Asia, is grown across Eurasia for both its feathery leaves and its seeds, both used to flavor food — what herb is it?
Dill (Anethum graveolens) is an annual herb in the celery family Apiaceae.
This group of 13 genetic connective tissue disorders causes loose joints, stretchy velvety skin, and abnormal scarring, sometimes leading to aortic dissection — name the condition?
Ehlers–Danlos syndrome (EDS) are a group of 13 genetic connective tissue disorders.
This recurring set of hormone-driven reproductive changes in female mammals is interrupted by 'rest' phases and pregnancy, and has a male equivalent called rut — what is it?

Estrous cycle (from Latin oestrus 'frenzy', originally from Ancient Greek (ostros) 'gadfly') is a set of recurring physiological changes induced by reproductive hormones in females of mammalian subclass Theria.

Sometimes mistakenly called a cat despite belonging to the weasel family, this North American forest-dwelling carnivore is the only living species in its genus and is larger than the martens it resembles — what animal is it?
Fisher (animal) (Pekania pennanti) is a carnivorous mammal native to North America, a forest-dwelling creature whose range covers much of the boreal forest in Canada to the northern United States.
Practitioners of this discipline monitor crustal motion, tides, and polar shifts to maintain accurate global positioning reference frames — what is this field called?
Geodesy (jee-) or geodetics is the science of measuring and representing the geometry, gravity, and spatial orientation of the Earth in temporally varying 3D space.
Flown by both the U.S. Navy and Britain's Royal Navy under the name Martlet, this 1940 carrier fighter went toe-to-toe with the Mitsubishi Zero over the Pacific — which aircraft?
Grumman F4F Wildcat is an American carrier-based fighter aircraft that entered service in 1940 with the United States Navy and the British Royal Navy.
Nicknamed the giant crab spider or cane spider, this member of the huntsman spider family is native to the tropics but has spread into subtropical areas — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria is a species of spider in the family Sparassidae, the huntsman spiders.

Ranging from mild headaches and poor balance to severe confusion and seizures, this low-blood-sodium condition can be triggered by causes as varied as vomiting, diuretics, or overhydration — what's it called?
Hyponatremia is a low concentration of sodium in the blood. It is generally defined as a sodium concentration of less than 135 mmol/L (135 mEq/L), with severe hyponatremia being below 120 mEq/L.
Part of the fig and mulberry family and thriving in tropical lowlands, this giant of the produce world can weigh as much as 55 kg and measures up to 90 cm long — what is it?
Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus) is a species of tree in the fig, mulberry, and breadfruit family (Moraceae).
This Columbia economist won the Nobel in 2001 and famously skewers his laissez-faire colleagues as "free-market fundamentalists" — who is he?
Joseph Stiglitz (born February 9, 1943) is an American New Keynesian economist, a public policy analyst, political activist, and a professor at Columbia University.
This genus of deciduous conifers, unusual for shedding its needles each year, dominates the boreal forests of Siberia and Canada, making it the most abundant tree genus on Earth — what is it called?
Larch are deciduous conifers in the genus Larix, of the family Pinaceae.
Named from the Greek word for 'stone,' this alkali metal with symbol Li tarnishes from silver to black in air and was once mined mainly from pegmatite minerals — what is it?
Lithium (from Ancient) is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

Native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere, this genus of 32 to 57 deciduous trees and shrubs in the rose family includes the ancestors of a familiar orchard fruit plus ornamental wild and crab varieties — what's the genus?
Malus (or) is a genus of about 32-57 species of small deciduous trees or shrubs in the family Rosaceae, including the domesticated orchard apple, crab apples, and wild apples.

This mammal family, uniting skunks and stink badgers, is defined by highly developed scent glands used to ward off predators, and was only split from the weasel family in the 1990s — what family is it?
Mephitidae is a family of mammals comprising the skunks and stink badgers.

Native to Africa, Asia, and Oceania, with one invasive species now in the southern U.S., this reptile genus ranges from 20 centimeters long to over 3 meters in the Komodo dragon — name this group of lizards?
Monitor lizard are lizards in the genus Varanus, the only extant genus in the family Varanidae.

Sometimes reaching two meters long but often thinner than a millimeter or two wide, these thread-like parasitoid worms turn up in damp puddles, troughs, and swimming pools as adults — what phylum is this?

Nematomorpha (sometimes called Gordiacea, and commonly known as horsehair worms, hairsnakes, or Gordian worms) are a phylum of parasitoid animals similar to yet distinct from nematode worms in morphology, hence the name.

Encompassing 24 genera from baboons to colobus to langurs, this is the largest primate family, having diverged from a separate primate lineage 45 to 55 million years ago before apes split off from it too — which family?
Old World monkey are primates in the family Cercopithecidae.

This inflammation of the skin around the nail is often triggered by frequent hand washing or cuticle trauma like nail biting, and is treated with antibiotics or antifungals depending on the cause — what condition is it?
Paronychia is an inflammation of the skin around the nail, often due to bacteria or fungi.

This insect order's scientific name derives from the Ancient Greek word for 'apparition' or 'phantom' — fitting for a group whose members are famous for disguising themselves as twigs and leaves. What order is this?
Phasmatodea (also known as Phasmida or Phasmatoptera) are an order of insects whose members are variously known as stick insects, stick bugs, walkingsticks, stick animals, or bug sticks.

This large, nearly ubiquitous family of flowering plants provides the world's cereal crops, bamboo, and the plants used in lawns and pastures, ranking as the fifth-largest plant family with roughly 12,000 species — what family is this?
Poaceae (poh-(y)e), also called Gramineae (gr-(y)e), is a large and nearly ubiquitous family of monocotyledonous flowering plants commonly known as true grasses.
This Eurasian fruit tree, also called the cherry plum, is believed to be one of the ancestral parents of the plum we cultivate today — what species is it?
Prunus cerasifera is a species of plum known by the common names cherry plum and myrobalan plum.
The only member of the genus Rangifer, this circumpolar deer of the Arctic tundra goes by another name entirely in North America — what is it?
Reindeer (Rangifer tarandus) is a species of deer with circumpolar distribution, native to Arctic, subarctic, tundra, boreal, and mountainous regions of Northern Europe, Siberia, and North America.

Grown mainly from Eastern and Northern Europe into Russia, this cold-tolerant grain crop is a member of the wheat tribe and its vigorous growth suppresses weeds while providing early forage for animals — name it?
Rye (Secale cereale) is a grass grown extensively as a grain, a cover crop and a forage crop.
Coined by Horace Walpole in 1754, this term describes an unplanned fortunate discovery, as with penicillin or the microwave oven — what is it called?
Serendipity is an unplanned fortunate discovery. The concept is often associated with scientific and technological breakthroughs, where accidental discoveries led to new insights or inventions.
This Polish-American Gestalt psychologist insisted 'most social acts lose meaning if isolated' — a credo that shaped his famous experiments on conformity and impression formation. Who was he?
Solomon Asch (September 14, 1907 - February 20, 1996) was a Polish-American Gestalt psychologist and pioneer in social psychology.
This colorless, sweet-smelling liquid with the formula C6H5CH=CH2 is manufactured from benzene as the industrial precursor to a widely used plastic — what compound is it?
Styrene is an organic compound with the chemical formula C6H5CH=CH2.

The primary male sex hormone and androgen, this hormone plays a key role in developing male reproductive tissues and secondary sexual characteristics like muscle, bone mass, and body hair. What is this hormone?

Testosterone is the primary male sex hormone and androgen in males. It is associated with increased aggression, sex drive, dominance, courtship display, and a wide range of behavioral characteristics.

Caused by the parasite Toxoplasma gondii and often spread through undercooked meat or contact with infected cat feces, this disease can be especially dangerous to a developing baby if a woman is infected during pregnancy — what is it?
Toxoplasmosis is a parasitic disease caused by Toxoplasma gondii, an apicomplexan.
This NBC science fiction drama series ran for three seasons and 30 episodes between 2021 and 2024, receiving mixed reviews from critics. What show is it?
Vasculitis is a group of disorders that destroy blood vessels by inflammation.

This bird family, which also includes piculets, wrynecks, and sapsuckers, is absent from Australia and Madagascar, though one desert-dwelling member has adapted to drill into cacti — what family of birds is it?
Woodpecker are part of the bird family Picidae, which also includes the piculets, wrynecks, and sapsuckers.
Formed when acetic acid combines with a base, this ion is also nature's most common building block for biosynthesis — what is it?
Acetate: Salt formed from acetic acid and a base.
Also known as thymol seeds, bishop's weed, or carom, this Apiaceae herb's fruit is often mistaken for lovage seed — what is it?
Nicknamed the death cap, this deadly poisonous fungus resembles edible species like Caesar's mushroom and is native to Europe — what is it?
Amanita phalloides: Poisonous mushroom (death cap). The large fruiting bodies appear in summer and autumn; the caps are generally greenish in colour with a white stipe and gills.

Multicellular eukaryotes that breathe oxygen and grow from a hollow ball of cells called a blastula, over 1.5 million species in this kingdom have been described by scientists. What are they collectively called?
Animal: Biological kingdom. Over 1.5 million living animal species have been described, of which around 1.05 million are insects, over 85,000 are molluscs, and around 65,000 are vertebrates.
Native to alpine lakes and polar coastal waters, this cold-water relative of salmon holds the title of the world's most northerly freshwater fish — what is it?
Sold as Lipitor, this first-line statin lowers cholesterol to fend off cardiovascular disease, with mild muscle aches among its better-known side effects — what's the drug?
A blood-feeding parasite of the genus Cimex that usually bites at night, this insect leaves itchy welts but, reassuringly, isn't known to spread any infectious disease — what is it?
Bed bug: Type of insect that feeds on human blood.
This class of aquatic molluscs — including clams, oysters, mussels, and scallops — has no head and encloses its soft body in a hinged pair of shells called valves — which class?
Bivalvia: Class of molluscs. The shell of a bivalve is composed of calcium carbonate, and consists of two, usually similar, parts called valves.

When a gas of bosons is cooled to within a hair of absolute zero, this state of matter, first predicted in 1924-25, sees a large fraction of particles pile into a single quantum state — what is it called?
Bose–Einstein condensate: State of matter. In 1995, the Bose–Einstein condensate was created by Eric Cornell and Carl Wieman of the University of Colorado Boulder using rubidium atoms.
Named after the Greek word for butter via butyric acid, this colorless, highly flammable gas exists as two isomers and vaporizes quickly at room temperature — what alkane is it?
Native to Africa, the Middle East, and arid parts of Asia, this nocturnal, secretive wild cat is built for the chase with long legs and dramatically long tufted ears — which animal?
Also called bachelor's button, this European annual once grew as a common weed among grain fields but is now endangered there due to herbicides — what flower is it?
Centaurea cyanus: Species of flowering plant.

Nicknamed for its spider-like look and also called airplane plant or hen and chicks, this houseplant is native to tropical Africa but can suffer 'burnt tips' from fluoride in tap water — which species?
Chlorophytum comosum: Species of flowering plant. It is native to tropical and Southern Africa but has become naturalized in other parts of the world, including Western Australia and Bangladesh.
Native to the Americas from Mexico to South America, this diurnal member of the Procyonidae family goes by the name 'quash' in Belize — what is it?

Known to NATO by the reporting name 'Mop' and to Canadian forces as the Canso, this WWII flying boat served every branch of the U.S. military and remained in some air forces into the 1980s — which aircraft?
Consolidated PBY Catalina: American 1930s flying boat.
This species includes honeydew, cantaloupe, and Casaba varieties, and traveled along ancient caravan routes long before its exact origin in the Levant or Egypt was ever confirmed — what fruit is it?
Cucumis melo: Species of plant. Cucumis melo, also known as melon or true melon, is a species of Cucumis that has been developed into many cultivated varieties.
Striking 48 to 72 hours after a heavy drinker's last drink, this potentially fatal condition brings hallucinations, seizures nicknamed 'rum fits,' and dangerously high body temperature — what is it?
Delirium tremens: Rapid onset of confusion caused by alcohol withdrawal.
Bred in Córdoba in the early 1900s to hunt wild boar and puma, this large mastiff-type breed's ancestry includes an extinct local fighting dog and a Bull Terrier — which breed is it?
Dogo Argentino: Argentine breed of dog. It was bred in the early twentieth century in Córdoba in central Argentina, primarily for hunting large game such as peccaries, wild boar, and pumas.
After stints at the CIA, Dell, and Booz Allen Hamilton, this NSA contractor flew to Hong Kong in 2013 and leaked thousands of classified documents exposing global surveillance — who is he?
Edward Snowden: Whistleblower and NSA contractor (born 1983)
One of the four basic animal tissue types, this thin protective cell layer lines blood vessels and body cavities and includes the skin's outer layer — what is it called?
Epithelium: Tissue lining the surfaces of organs in animals.
In this small bird of prey, females can be up to 25% larger than males — one of the biggest size gaps between sexes of any bird — and it hunts garden songbirds across Europe and Asia — which raptor?

Eurasian sparrowhawk: Species of bird. The Eurasian sparrowhawk (Accipiter nisus), also known as the northern sparrowhawk or simply the sparrowhawk, is a small bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.
Likely domesticated from the European polecat, with which it can still interbreed to produce hybrids, this slender mustelid averages about 50 centimeters long — what is it?
With atomic number 87 and a most stable isotope whose half-life is just 22 minutes, this alkali metal is the second-rarest naturally occurring element on Earth — which one?
Francium: Chemical element with atomic number 87 (Fr)

Born as an air-superiority day fighter and now, as of 2026, the world's most common military fixed-wing aircraft with over 4,600 built, this single-engine jet flies on as the 'Viper' family — which aircraft?
General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon: American multi-role fighter aircraft.
With the symbol Au and atomic number 79, this soft, dense element is so unreactive that only platinum sits below it — and it often turns up as native nuggets in riverbeds. What is it?
Gold: Chemical element with atomic number 79 (Au). Chemically, gold is a transition metal, a group 11 element, and one of the noble metals.
Combined with obstetrics as a joint medical specialty and touching on everything from family planning to pelvic reconstructive surgery, which field focuses on the female reproductive system?
Gynaecology: Medical area for women's reproductive health.
This Dutch-born entrepreneur produced Japan's first major turn-based role-playing game and later secured the console distribution rights to a Russian puzzle game called Tetris — who is he?
Henk Rogers: Dutch-born American computer programmer (born 1953)
Despite the name, this 'living fossil' is no crustacean at all — it's a chelicerate, kin to spiders and scorpions, and its three-part body ends in a spiky tail called a telson. What creature is it?
Horseshoe crab: Family of basal chelicerates.
This mammal order today includes only small African and Middle Eastern hyraxes, but once boasted a species weighing up to 600 kilograms called Titanohyrax — which order?
Hyracoidea: Order of mammals. It includes the living hyraxes, placed within the family Procaviidae, and several extinct taxa.
She and her husband won the 1935 Nobel in Chemistry for discovering induced radioactivity — making her half of the only mother-daughter pair to both win Nobel Prizes. Who is this scientist?
Irène Joliot-Curie: French chemist and physicist (1897–1956)

This temporary condition throws your internal body clock out of sync with local time after rapid travel across multiple time zones — and most people find it harder to shake off flying east than west — what is it?

Jet lag: Condition due to travel across time zones. The phase shift when travelling from east to west is referred to as phase-delay of the circadian cycle, whereas going west to east is phase-advance of the cycle.

Known to NATO by the reporting name Hokum A and nicknamed 'Black Shark' for its distinctive coaxial rotors, this Russian single-seat attack helicopter has a rare rescue ejection system — which aircraft?
Kamov Ka-50: Attack helicopter. It was designed in the 1980s and adopted for service in the Russian army in 1995.
Sold under the brand name Lamictal, this medication treats epilepsy and helps stabilize mood in bipolar disorder — what is it?

Lamotrigine: Anticonvulsant medication. Lamotrigine ( luh-MOH-trih-jeen), sold under the brand name Lamictal among others, is a medication used to treat epilepsy and stabilize mood in bipolar disorder.
Formed by cross-linking phenolic precursors, this class of complex organic polymers gives rigidity to plant cell walls, especially in wood and bark — what is it?
Lignin: Structural phenolic polymer in plant cell walls.
Native to Afghanistan and Iran, this herb tastes like an intensified cross between celery and parsley, with seeds used much like fennel — what is it?
This sexually dimorphic East Asian perching waterfowl, closely related to North America's wood-dwelling cousin, gets its species name from a Latin word for a wig — which bird?
Mandarin duck: Species of bird. The mandarin duck (Aix galericulata) is a perching duck species native to East and Northeast Asia.
This cone-shaped part of the brainstem controls involuntary functions from sneezing to heart rate, and was once known simply as 'the bulb' — which structure?
Medulla oblongata: Structure of the brain stem.
Grouped by their small size and use of echolocation, this suborder of flying mammals turns out to be genetically distinct from its bigger, fruit-eating relatives — which creatures?

There's a large introduced population of this small carnivorous mammal in Hawaii, though its family — split into the Herpestinae and Mungotinae — is native to southern Europe, Africa, and Asia — what animal is it?

Mongoose: Family of mammals in Africa and Asia. The Herpestinae comprises 23 living species that are native to southern Europe, Africa and Asia, whereas the Mungotinae comprises 11 species native to Africa.

When light from distant objects focuses in front of the retina rather than on it, far-away things blur while close ones stay sharp — and spending more time outdoors as a child seems to lower the risk. What's this refractive error?
Myopia: Inability to focus on distant objects.
This small sauropod dinosaur had a wide muzzle packed with more than 500 teeth that were replaced roughly every two weeks — what genus is it?
Native to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, this striped mammal looks like a zebra crossbred with a giraffe but is actually the giraffe's closest living relative — which animal?
Okapi: Species of mammal. Although the okapi has striped markings reminiscent of zebras, it is most closely related to the giraffe.
